3L.16 You should not refuse to be corrected and reproved by the righteous among you.

precepts.text: Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil, which shall not break my head. Somebody telling you that you are doing evil is not going to kill you. It is supposed to kill the old man in you, not you. When you come to this truth, prepare your soul for temptation; it starts unmasking who you are and what we have to fix.
precepts.point: For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty. That is the breath that was breathed into us in Genesis 2. If those are the attributes of wisdom, you want to be tethered to wisdom, so you can discern, so you understand why people do the things they do, so you know the intents of a person's heart when they speak.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Converting comes through trial, error and correction, and you're supposed to be happy about the correction. “Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness”: when that person is telling you what you're doing wrong, it's a kindness that he does it. “and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil”: it's going to be a blessing.

“which shall not break my head.” It isn't going to kill you. Somebody telling you that you are doing evil is not going to kill you. It's supposed to kill the old man in you, not you physically. And people don't want to hear that; they don't want to know the errors of their ways.

When you come to this truth, prepare your soul for temptations, for trials, for tribulation. People come in with rose-colored glasses, thinking everything's going to be perfect. No: it's going to start unmasking who you are, who I am, and what we have to fix to get right. It's sweet until you start dealing with who you really are. That is the wisdom that leadeth and directeth the wise, as Solomon says: God directs you away from evil and shows you how to avoid it, and his reproof is how he does it.

precepts.text: Let the righteous smite me, it shall be an excellent oil which shall not break my head; correction is oil for the lamp.
precepts.point: Though Israel is in captivity now without a temple, without lamps to bring oil for, and no longer under the Levitical priesthood, think about it spiritually: you have to keep your lamp lit and keep the oil in your life. Brotherhood and unity, and correction, which is an excellent oil that shall not break the head, are that oil; if you are not around a body being built up and corrected by teachers and peers, that is how people run out of oil, their lamp goes out, and they fall out of this truth and do not endure to the end. The ten virgins with their lamps and oil come to mind here, offered as a meditation.

note.label: Exodus 27: The Altar, the Court, and the Oil for the Lamp

precepts.why:
“Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil, which shall not break my head: for yet my prayer also shall be in their calamities.”

Correction is oil for the lamp, an excellent oil that shall not break the head. Being corrected by teachers and peers in a body that is being built up is what keeps the oil in your life. Without it the lamp goes out, and people fall out of this truth and do not endure to the end.

precepts.text: Let the righteous smite me, it shall be a kindness; even the bones broken by correction will rejoice because in the end you get yourself right.
precepts.point: Make me to hear joy and gladness, that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice. This does not mean the Most High literally broke his bones; it means correction.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.” This does not mean the Most High literally broke David's bones; it means correction. David says the same in Psalm 141: “Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil, which shall not break my head”.

Being smitten and reproved by the righteous is a kindness and an excellent oil. Even the bones broken by correction will rejoice, because in the end you get yourself right. That is the joy and gladness David asks to hear.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; there is a law set up for how we govern ourselves.
precepts.point: He asks the Lord not to let his heart be inclined to practice wicked works with men that work iniquity, and not to let him eat of their dainties, meaning not to partake or follow the wicked to do evil.

note.label: Psalm 141: A Prayer to Be Kept From Evil

precepts.why:
“Incline not my heart to any evil thing, to practise wicked works with men that work iniquity: and let me not eat of their dainties.” Not eating of their dainties means not partaking or following the wicked to do evil. “Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment”. There is a law set up for how we govern ourselves.

David also asks for a watch before his mouth and the door of his lips kept, help to control his mouth, the same as James telling us to bridle the tongue; and that his heart not be inclined to evil, that his mind and spirit not go after evil things but walk in the spirit.

points: David cries to the Lord to make haste to him and to hear his voice, asking that his prayer be set before the Lord as incense and the lifting up of his hands as the evening sacrifice.

note.label: Psalm 141: A Prayer to Be Kept From Evil

points: Set a watch before my mouth, keep the door of my lips: this is asking the Lord to help him control his mouth, the same as James telling us to bridle the tongue.

note.label: Psalm 141: A Prayer to Be Kept From Evil

points: Incline not my heart to any evil thing means do not let my mind and my spirit go after things that are evil; help me walk in the spirit.

He asks the Lord not to let his heart be inclined to practice wicked works with men that work iniquity, and not to let him eat of their dainties, meaning not to partake or follow the wicked to do evil.

note.label: Psalm 141: A Prayer to Be Kept From Evil

points: Now David says the opposite. Instead of being inclined to work evil, he asks that the righteous correct him, and that correction is counted as kindness and love.
Correction may be uncomely and it will not be very comely, but it is for good; it shall not break his head, meaning it is not going to hurt him. When you get corrected, that is kindness.
A danger he names is envying the wicked, because a lot of times we envy those in the world when nothing seems to be happening to them.

note.label: Psalm 141: A Prayer to Be Kept From Evil

points: David trusts the Lord and asks that his soul not be left destitute, that he be kept from the snares and gins the workers of iniquity have laid, and that the wicked fall into their own nets while he escapes.
